facts.text: Bedford Park was planned with 40 suburban homes on 23 acres, called Villa Avenue.
The neighborhood was named Bedford Park after a London suburb, and developers built a suburban retreat 20 years after a sale.
Bedford Park’s early streets were curved and marketed for healthful air near the then‑planning Bronx Park, home to the future zoo and botanical garden.
The 1890s extension of the Third Avenue Elevated Line and the opening of Bedford Park Station on the Harlem Line anchored the community’s early accessibility.
Lehman College, originally Hunter College’s uptown campus, sits on the Grand Concourse and is a notable landmark in Bedford Park.
The Bedford Mosholu Community Association, founded in 1975, has championed safety, cleanliness, and civic engagement while welcoming diverse residents.
